catalog_locator: 2024 sketch §5 'Prosodic word, syllable structure, and stress', pp. 25-31; deciding passage p. 27 (Table 3), summary sentence p. 31; saved file (+, 945-946, 968-970). General rule: Hernández Luna 2021 §3 pp. 15-17, 503-505, 555-557, 561-566 (ex. 9).
catalog_quote: Even though zam is a monosyllabic language, there are disyllabic morphologically complex words that reveal an iambic stress pattern. The stressed syllable is always heavy while unstressed syllables are always light (Sicoli 2007; Arellanes 2021, among others). This means that bimoraicity is related to both stress and minimality. The prosodic requirement that the minimal word be a bimoraic foot, even when it is a monosyllable, is because a stressed syllable is bimoraic and a prosodic word must have a stressed syllable. Table 3 shows the words [kàː] ‘to move’ and [níː] ‘foot’ in isolation, and finally the compound [kàníː] ‘to dance’. The compound word is formed by an unbalanced iambic foot, a canonical iamb according to Hayes (1995). ... In sum, the most prominent cue of stress in Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec is the duration of the rhyme.

Section 5 'Prosodic word, syllable structure, and stress' runs pp. 25-31 as stated. The quoted passage is on p. 27, every sentence found verbatim (checked sentence by sentence against extracted text output); the only difference is that the quote silently drops one sentence between sentences 2 and 3 ('This means that bimoraicity is related to both stress and minimality.') without an ellipsis. Surrounding section read: p. 25-26 lexicon mostly monosyllabic, minimal word = bimoraic foot; p. 27 Table 3 [kàː] + [níː] > [kàníː] 'to dance', unbalanced iambic foot; pp.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The lexicon is overwhelmingly monosyllabic; each prosodic word has exactly one stressed syllable, which is bimoraic (long vowel, or vowel + moraic fortis/sonorant coda). In the polysyllabic words that exist (compounds, na- stative forms, Spanish loans) stress is iambic: it falls on the final syllable of the base, i.e. the right edge of the prosodic word, with preceding syllables light and unstressed. The same author's 2021 CLECM article (same Santo Domingo de Morelos data) states it directly: 'el acento siempre caerá en la sílaba del borde derecho de la base' (p. 17), with right-to-left directionality shown by recursive compounds [jí.síd.ŋɡùð.ˈlòː] 'pestaña'. Acoustic correlate is rhyme duration (stressed rhyme ~2x unstressed), not vowel duration, intensity or F0 (F0 = tone). The language is tonal (H, L, falling, rising) with stress alongside tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described. Beam de Azcona 2016 (San Bartolomé Loxicha Miahuatec slides) raises '¿acento secundario?' for first roots of compounds that retain their tone, without deciding.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for the position. Bimoraicity is obligatory and culminative (max one bimoraic syllable per word; Hernández Luna 2021 p. 16). Enclitics fall outside the prosodic word (Beam de Azcona 2016: 'los clíticos son extramétricos'; Beam & Cruz Santiago 2022 §2.1). Loans: [mer.kaːð] 'mercado', [ku.tʃiː] 'caballo' with final lengthening (Hernández Luna 2020: 159).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: prosodic word = base (root plus any preceding prefix/compound member), enclitics excluded; statements are based on elicited isolation forms and compounds (109 words x 3 repetitions, two speakers of Santo Domingo de Morelos, Hernández Luna 2021 §3.1; three speakers, fieldwork 2008-2019, for the 2024 sketch). Unstressed (pretonic) syllables lose contrastive tone, glottalization and coda contrasts.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding sources describe the Santo Domingo de Morelos variety (Pochutla district). The authors label it 'Miahuatec Zapotec (ISO zam)', but Glottolog 5.1 files Hernández Luna's Santo Domingo de Morelos work under loxi1235 (ztp Loxicha Zapotec), and Beam de Azcona & Cruz Santiago 2022 (§2) state that Santo Domingo de Morelos 'pertenece a la misma zona dialectal de San Agustín Loxicha' (the ztp reference town), treating SAL/SDM and San Bartolomé Loxicha (zam) as one language, 'miahuateco'. So the statement is first-hand for a ztp town but is framed by its authors as Miahuatec; the group-level rule (final stress of the lexical word, clitics extrametrical) is independently stated for San Bartolomé Loxicha [zam] by Beam de Azcona 2016/2022. No stress statement specifically for San Agustín Loxicha was found (Beam de Azcona 2008 gives only tentative tones for SAL; Salminen 2014 not accessible).

sources.note: SBarL [zam]: one stressed syllable per prosodic word (Hyman's stress accent); 'la sílaba que corresponde a la última raíz es la más prominente' (duration, intensity); prosodic word = tonic syllable + preceding pretonic syllables, enclitics excluded. Identity: Santo Domingo de Morelos belongs to the San Agustín Loxicha dialect zone; SAL/SDM and SBarL one language.
